cases.purpose: Exercise byte normalization, long command lines, listing, delimiters, and no-match status on controlled proc records.
cases.oracle: Literal NUL-separated synthetic proc records and the pgrep command-line output contract.
cases.script:
set -e
mkdir -p proc/810001 proc/810002 proc/810003 proc/810004
export BASHOS_PROC_ROOT=$PWD/proc
printf 'one\n' > proc/810001/comm
printf 'two\n' > proc/810002/comm
printf 'long\n' > proc/810003/comm
printf 'empty\n' > proc/810004/comm
printf 'one\000line\nbreak\000tab\there\000\000end\000' > proc/810001/cmdline
printf 'two\000arg\000' > proc/810002/cmdline
printf 'long\000' > proc/810003/cmdline
printf '%06000d' 0 >> proc/810003/cmdline
printf 'TAIL\000' >> proc/810003/cmdline
: > proc/810004/cmdline
pgrep -af -x $'one line break tab\there  end'
pgrep -l -x one
pgrep -f 'TAIL$'
pgrep -af 'TAIL$' > long.out
[[ $(wc -c < long.out) == 6017 ]]
printf 'long-output-size=6017\n'
pgrep -d, -x 'one|two' > joined
v=$(<joined)
[[ $v == 810001,810002 || $v == 810002,810001 ]]
printf 'delimiter=ok\n'
pgrep -c -f 'no_such_cmdline' || rc=$?
printf 'status=%s\n' "${rc:-0}"
cases.stdout:
810001 one line break tab	here  end
810001 one
810003
long-output-size=6017
delimiter=ok
0
status=1
